title: Postselection-loophole-free Bell test under strict spacetime constraints
authors: Kannan Vijayadharan, Matías Rubén Bolaños, Andrea Pompermaier, Tommaso Bertapelle, Francesco B. L. Santagiustina, Costantino Agnesi, Giuseppe Vallone, Paolo Villoresi
abstract: Entanglement gives rise to correlations between distant quantum systems that cannot be explained by local realistic theories. Bell inequality violations provide a direct way to reveal these correlations and certify nonlocality, especially when the relevant experimental loopholes are closed. Time-bin encoding, in which quantum information is encoded into well-defined temporal modes, is a commonly used platform for distributing photonic entanglement in optical fibers. Yet loophole-free Bell tests with time-bin entanglement have received comparatively little attention, owing in part to the postselection loophole introduced by conventional interferometric measurements. Here, we demonstrate a fiber-based platform for Bell tests with time-bin entanglement that simultaneously closes the locality, freedom-of-choice, and postselection loopholes. We observe a CHSH violation of $S=2.583 \pm 0.002$, exceeding the local-realistic bound by over 265 standard deviations. Notably, this rigorous certification of nonlocality is achieved at a separation distance of $49.0 \pm 0.7$ m, substantially shorter than previous photonic Bell tests addressing comparable space-time constraints. Beyond its foundational significance, our results demonstrate time-bin entanglement as a viable route towards practical device-independent quantum communication and a future quantum internet.
summary: This paper reports a significant experimental achievement in quantum physics by demonstrating a loophole-free Bell test using time-bin entangled photons over a 49-meter distance. By employing a novel Sagnac-modulator architecture, the authors successfully eliminated the postselection loophole, confirming nonlocality with a high violation of the CHSH inequality. The results establish time-bin entanglement as a robust platform for practical quantum communication.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of performing loophole-free Bell tests using time-bin entangled photons while operating under strict spacetime constraints.
main_result: They successfully demonstrated a loophole-free Bell test achieving a CHSH violation of S = 2.583 ± 0.002 at a separation distance of 49.0 m, closing locality, freedom-of-choice, and postselection loopholes.
method: The experiment utilizes a fiber-based platform with a Sagnac-modulator architecture to perform postselection-free measurements on time-bin entangled photons.
model_or_system: The system uses time-bin encoding of photonic entanglement generated via SPDC, measured using customized fiber-coupled unbalanced Mach-Zehnder interferometers (uMZIs). The analysis incorporates a (2+1D) spacetime formalism to rigorously check loophole closure conditions.

important_parameters: Separation distance of 49.0 ± 0.7 m; CHSH violation exceeding the local-realistic bound by over 265 standard deviations.
main_assumptions: The authors explicitly note that the detection loophole remains open due to current technological limitations in achieving required overall detection efficiency.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the experimental layout (Source, Alice, Bob) and the detailed scheme of the fast optical switch used for postselection-free measurement.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the scientific problem (loophole-free Bell tests with time-bin entanglement) to detailing the advanced hardware implementation (Sagnac switch for postselection removal), followed by rigorous characterization of timing and randomness sources.
why_interesting: This work provides a highly practical, device-independent demonstration of nonlocality using time-bin entanglement, which is crucial for advancing quantum communication protocols and quantum internet infrastructure.
